Alaska.Ai — Anchorage Desk Draft

2026-06-24 · branch claude/linkedin-desk-2026-06-24
No defensible target this cycle. The desk ran the full discovery and validation pipeline and cleared no subject through the seven-point anti-puff gate. Nothing shipped, by design, rather than risk a puff piece.

Why nothing shipped

The sole in-window candidate (Billy Wailand / GCI-Starlink bonded gateway deployment, 2026-06-11) failed Gate 3 decisively: the primary source contains no mention of AI, and neither independent corroborator (Telecompetitor, Broadband Breakfast) connects this decision to any AI application, model, or data strategy. The AI nexus cited by the scout is upstream-narrative only. GCI's separate Databricks adoption (Troy Goldie, 2026-03-16) is a distinct decision, out of window, and a different subject. Treating any telecom infrastructure vendor selection as an Alaska AI decision would collapse the column's mandate. A 45-day broadening was evaluated: scouts already confirmed no AI-specific decisions exist in the 2026-05-10 to 2026-05-24 band beyond the out-of-window items listed (all dated before 2026-05-10 or otherwise excluded). Broadening yields zero additional candidates. No defensible target this cycle.

Scout coverage

  • founders — returned 0 in-window candidates (exhaustive sweep)
  • operators — returned 1 in-window candidate (GCI/Starlink), failed validator Gate 3
  • municipal — returned 0 in-window candidates (exhaustive sweep)
  • research — returned 0 in-window candidates (exhaustive sweep)

Dropped candidates

  • Billy Wailand (SVP Corporate Development, GCI)
    GCI Starlink bonded-gateway network resiliency deployment (2026-06-11)
    Gate 3 fail. Decision is telecom infrastructure resiliency (Starlink bonded gateway vendor selection), not an Alaska AI decision. Primary source contains zero mention of AI, machine learning, or data strategy. Both fetched corroborators confirm the same. The AI tie cited by the scout is narrative-upstream via a separate, out-of-window Databricks decision owned by a different executive (Troy Goldie, 2026-03-16). Promoting a telecom infrastructure contract as an AI decision would convert the column into a connectivity puff piece.
  • Anchorage AI founders slice (Erik Williams/beadedcloud, Lorenzo Chu/Arcnito, Jay Byam/Kartorium, et al.)
    various cohort / pitch / accelerator events
    All documentable decisions fall outside the 30-day and 45-day windows (March-April 2026 accelerator cohort and pitch events). 'Sovereign Sensors' Series A dropped as an AI-generated listicle with no primary source. Sparrow Mahoney / STAK Energy permanently blocked.
  • Anchorage municipal slice (Perez-Verdia / Rivera et al.)
    AO 2026-27 data center zoning ordinance (10-2 vote, 2026-03-27)
    Strongest municipal AI-adjacent decision is ~60 days out of window. The only in-window Assembly action with technology adjacency (AO 2026-62 public safety commission 8-4 postponement, June 9-10) is a procedural delay, not an AI/data/tech procurement or policy decision.
  • Anchorage research slice (UAA FIF awardees; NSF AI-UNITE/RAISE PIs; ANTHC/SCF symposium authors)
    AI faculty grants / symposium paper
    FIF awards announced 2026-02-12 (out of window). NSF awards predate window. ANTHC/SCF symposium paper published 2026-05-23, two days before window opens, and no Anchorage-based author owns a specific AI implementation binary (corresponding author Stanford-based).

Editor's note

No subagent stalled. All four scouts (founders, operators, municipal, research) returned within the wall-clock limit. Three of four slices returned zero in-window candidates; the operators slice returned one (GCI/Starlink), which the validator failed on Gate 3 (decision is telecom infrastructure, not an Alaska AI decision). The validator evaluated a 45-day broadening per the retry rule and confirmed it yields zero additional AI-specific candidates. No image was rendered and no post was written, consistent with a no-target cycle. The conflict-of-interest screen was not reached (no candidate cleared the seven-point gate). Note: the prior four desk cycles (2026-05-21, 05-28, 06-04, 06-18) were also no-target; only 2026-05-20 shipped a profile. The Anchorage AI subject pool is small and primary-source AI decisions are low-frequency, so quiet cycles are expected calibration, not a failure.
